The Senior Manager, NPI will be expected to provide technical input to the leadership team to support business decisions.
  
  
This leader, with their team develops and implements operations requirements for design transfer across all product portfolios and collaborates with development, manufacturing and technical support teams to assure that all aspects of design for quality and manufacturability (DQM) are utilized for robust design development, transfer and ultimately scale up. Assures appropriate test method validations and product specifications are developed and implemented. Individual is also responsible for managing new part number creation and appropriate work instruction development. Will work cross functionally to ensure repeatability and reproducibility of the manufactured products within product and process capabilities and meeting of desired specifications.

* Establishes overall team direction and goals, and sets direction of resources toward completion of goals, in conjunction with Senior Leadership in both Development and Operations. Promotes an open, collaborative environment focused on teamwork

* Establish group and individual objectives, priorities, and metrics
* Ensure production of products meets expected output
* Ensure quality requirements are fulfilled and maintained
* Provide technical support for failure analysis and root cause investigation of product failures.
* Analyze manufacturing lines from a risk perspective (pFMEA) to incorporate and validate critical tests used in manufacturing.
* Assume responsibility for the validation of manufacturing equipment and processes leveraging standard qualification approaches (IQ/OQ/PQ/DQ/PPQ).
* Provide production line support for day-to-day engineering issues on production and NPI lines.
* Identify and implement continuous improvement projects with respect to first pass yield, cycle time reduction, product reliability, capacity enhancements, and cost reduction.
* Liaise between project management, engineering, and manufacturing functions to ensure project goals are on track
* Adherence to applicable QMS policies and procedures
* Ensure the team sets and meets reasonable deliverable expectations Review and approve engineering changes
* Facilitate problem-solving efforts and continually improve processes
* Understand, lead, and coach in DFX concepts, pFMEA, problem-solving, and transfer efforts
* Lead in the decision-making process for production planning and layout
* Evaluate and estimate the required and proposed engineering tasks (headcount or hours) Understand the product funnel and needs for NPI resources during the early phases of development

**Requirements**

* Minimum of 15 years of demonstrated experience in people management and leadership role
* Minimum of 10 years experience in electronics manufacturing and knowledge of Design Control guidelines
* Minimum of 10 years leading/managing New Product Introduction Teams; including hiring, employee development, managing subordinate managers, project planning, and coordination in a matrixed organization

* Excellent time management, planning, organization and problem solving skills
* Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor and coach team members

Build Your Career as a Director, Operational Excellence & Business Enablement!
  
  
At BlueLinx, our people are at the heart of our success. We are committed to ensuring our team members can build job security, enhance their skills, and make meaningful contributions. We deliver the building blocks to better lives.
  
  
Join us and be part of a company that values its people and strives to make a positive impact on the industry!
  
  
**Why BlueLinx?**
**Comprehensive Benefits Include**

* Medical, Dental, Vision, Prescription
* 401(k) with company match
* Tuition reimbursement
* Life Insurance
* Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and 8 Company Holidays
* Career Growth: Opportunity to develop and advance your career with a leading building products distributor.

**Job Summary**
The Director, Operational Excellence & Business Enablement leads the development and deployment of the BlueLinx operating system across the branch network. This role converts operational strategy, performance data, and technology investments into standard processes, measurable performance improvement, and sustained branch adoption. Reporting to the Sr. Director, Logistics Systems, the Director partners across Regional Operations, Branch Operations, Commercial, Inventory, Finance, Human Resources, Safety, and Information Technology to improve customer service, labor productivity, cost performance, process consistency, and the adoption of new operating capabilities.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Understands the company’s vision, mission, and strategy; translates business and functional objectives into clear Operational Excellence priorities and measurable outcomes.
* Leads the enterprise operations performance-management process, including metric definitions, monthly reporting, trend analysis, performance reviews, corrective-action follow-up, and continuous improvement of dashboards and reporting methods.
* Owns governance and continuous improvement for On-Time and In-Full delivery performance, including failure-reason categories, functional ownership, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and branch adoption.
* Develops and maintains the BlueLinx branch operating system, including standard work, daily and weekly management routines, branch assessment methods, operating playbooks, and sustainment reviews.
* Leads the operational labor-management strategy, including common productivity measures, labor standards, reporting requirements, and branch improvement plans developed in partnership with Regional Operations and Human Resources.
* Serves as the business process and adoption leader for operations, logistics and warehouse technology-enabled improvement initiatives, including transportation, warehouse management, scanning, labeling, automation, data, and artificial intelligence capabilities.
* Translates operational needs into clear business requirements; leads current-state and future-state process design, operational pilots, field testing, readiness, rollout planning, training, adoption measurement, and post-launch sustainment.
* Maintains the enterprise Operational Excellence project portfolio and prioritizes work based on customer impact, business value, risk, available resources, and alignment with company strategy.
* Partners with Finance to validate expected and realized financial benefits, including direct savings, cost avoidance, productivity improvements, and working-capital opportunities.
* Provides structured problem-solving support for complex, cross-functional, or recurring branch issues while ensuring the accountable function retains ownership of execution and sustainment.
* Builds organizational capability through practical training and coaching in standard work, root-cause analysis, process improvement, visual management, and leader operating routines.
* Identifies proven branch practices and creates repeatable methods to scale those practices across regions and locations.
* Builds strong working relationships with regional, branch, and functional leadership; influences decisions through clear data, practical recommendations, and disciplined follow-through.
* Leads and develops assigned Operational Excellence, analytics, process improvement, or industrial engineering resources and actively supports talent acquisition and succession planning.
* Travel: Up to 50%, based on branch support, project deployment, leader development, and business priorities

**Qualifications**

* Certifications: Lean, Six Sigma Black Belt, or comparable process-improvement certification preferred
* Educational: Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Business, or a related field required. Master's degree preferred.
* Generally 5+ years of relevant experience in distribution, manufacturing, logistics, or multi-site operations; demonstrated experience leading people and cross-functional business process improvement

**What We're Looking For**

* Deep knowledge of distribution or multi-site operations, including branch execution, warehouse processes, customer service, labor productivity, and operating cost drivers.
* Demonstrated ability to build performance-management systems that connect measures, root causes, ownership, corrective action, and sustained results.
* Practical experience developing standard work, management routines, branch assessments, and scalable operating playbooks.
* Experience leading cross-functional improvement initiatives from business requirements and process design through pilot, rollout, adoption, and sustainment.
* Strong business analytics capability with the ability to validate data, interpret performance, identify meaningful trends, and communicate findings in plain language.
* Working knowledge of warehouse and transportation technology, business intelligence tools, automation, and technology-enabled process improvement.
* Experience with labor management, industrial engineering, warehouse layout, slotting, material flow, or labor standards preferred.
* Strong facilitation, project leadership, change-management, coaching, and executive communication skills.
* Ability to move comfortably between branch-level observation and executive-level decision support.
* Ability to manage competing priorities, establish decision rights, and prevent temporary project support from becoming permanent functional ownership
* Strong follow-through, sound judgment, and a bias toward simple, repeatable solutions that can be sustained by the field.

Our Values
  
  
With every decision and action, we put people first, keep the future in mind, and work as a team toward shared progress.
  
  

* Customer Centric
* Respect
* Collaboration
* Integrity
* Grit

**About Us**
BlueLinx is one of America’s largest distributors of building products, with over 70k branded and private-label SKUs. Headquartered in Marietta, Georgia, we have over 2,000 associates and distribute our comprehensive range of structural and specialty products to approximately 15k national, regional, and local dealers, as well as specialty distributors, national home centers, industrial, and manufactured housing customers.
  
  
*The salary range provided is a good-faith estimate based on the position requirements and market data. Actual compensation will depend on factors including experience, qualifications, skills, geographic location, and other job-related considerations. BlueLinx also offers a comprehensive benefits package including health care, dental, vision, life and disability insurance starting the first day of the month, 15 days of paid time off that start accruing your first day, and 8 paid holidays per year.*

**About Komline**

As a pioneering leader in advanced separation technologies, Komline has established a global reputation for engineering excellence. Through our combination of innovative design, cutting-edge manufacturing capabilities, and decades of industry experience, we consistently deliver the highest quality equipment from our integrated manufacturing facilities. Serving our core markets of Water & Process, Agricultural & Renewables, and Industrials, we pride ourselves on providing comprehensive separation solutions precisely tailored to our clients' requirements. With a strong track record of strategic growth and acquisitions, Komline continues to expand its solution portfolio and technical capabilities while maintaining our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction.

**This Opportunity**

The Director, Operational Excellence is responsible for building, deploying, and sustaining the Komline Business System (KBS), a consistent operating excellence system across all Komline sites. This leader will partner with Business Unit General Managers, Plant Managers, and functional leaders to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, working capital, productivity, and overall operating discipline while respecting the P&L accountability of each business. The role will lead Komline’s enterprise continuous improvement (CI) capability, develop CI talent, and ensure proven practices are shared and scaled across the network.

The successful candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who combines strong Lean expertise with business judgment, credibility on the shop floor, and the executive presence to influence decentralized business leaders. This leader will be equally comfortable coaching a plant team, challenging a site improvement plan, and communicating enterprise priorities to senior leadership.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this enterprise-wide role supports all Komline operating sites.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

* Develop and lead implementation of the KBS Operational Excellence strategy, roadmap, standards, and multi-year improvement agenda across all sites
* Lead, coach, and develop the CI Manager team and other improvement resources; establish clear site coverage, priorities, and deployment expectations
* Partner with GMs and Plant Managers to identify the highest-impact opportunities and build robust, financially validated site-level improvement pipelines that deliver sustained results in safety, productivity, delivery, lead time, quality, inventory, cost, and working capital
* Establish and sustain common Lean / KBS operating practices, including daily management, visual management, standard work, problem solving, RCCM, value-stream improvement, kaizen, and leader standard work
* Create a practical maturity assessment for Operational Excellence and use it to prioritize coaching, capability building, and site support; track improvements in maturity and consistent adoption of core operating practices
* Drive measurable productivity and capacity improvements through flow, labor optimization, constraint removal, setup reduction, layout improvement, and waste elimination
* Partner with Industrial Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, EHS, Finance, Engineering, HR, and other enterprise functions to quantify benefits and ensure improvements are sustained
* Build CI capability within site leadership and frontline teams through training, coaching, kaizen leadership, and development of local change agents
* Establish common operational KPI definitions and review routines that enable benchmarking and the sharing and scaling of best practices across Komline
* Support acquisition integration by assessing operational maturity, identifying improvement opportunities, and integrating acquired sites into Komline’s operating system
* Provide regular enterprise-level reporting to the COO on CI pipeline, benefits realization, site maturity, risks, and resource priorities
* Promote a culture of accountability, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement while maintaining strong partnership with decentralized business leadership

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, continuous improvement, operational excellence, industrial engineering, or related leadership roles
* Demonstrated success leading Lean / continuous improvement across multiple sites or business units
* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing, daily management, kaizen, standard work, value-stream mapping, structured problem solving, and performance management
* Proven ability to influence GMs, Plant Managers, and functional leaders without relying on direct authority
* Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to translate operational improvements into measurable financial impact
* Excellent leadership, coaching, facilitation, communication, and executive presentation skills
* Ability to travel approximately 50%+, depending on site and project needs

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Lean leadership certification or equivalent and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt
* Experience in multi-site industrial, engineered-product, capital-equipment, or process-equipment manufacturing
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or deploying a common operating system across decentralized businesses
* Experience with plant layout, flow optimization, capacity improvement, and working-capital initiatives
* MBA or advanced technical/operations degree

**Equal Opportunity Statement:**
Komline is an EEO employer – M/F/Vets/Disabled

Restek is looking for a builder. As our Director of Continuous Improvement, you’ll stand up an enterprise-wide continuous improvement program, developing the systems, the talent, and the Lean culture that make operational excellence part of how we work every day across Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Customer Experience.

Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, you’ll be our principal change agent, leading everything from multi-year transformation programs to focused Kaizen events. Your work will directly shape our strategic priorities by reducing waste and scrap, raising quality, speeding flow, improving the customer experience, and growing profitability.

**What You’ll Do**

Set the Strategy

* Own the multi-year CI roadmap, aligned with Restek’s strategic plan, annual operating plan, and Operations priorities.
* Establish the management system that makes improvement stick (daily management, tiered huddles, A3 problem solving) and define a CI maturity model to guide each function’s progress.
* Partner with Finance to validate savings and ensure improvement gains show up in the P&L.

Lead the Work

* Personally lead and facilitate high-impact Kaizen events, Value Stream Mapping, and transformation projects tied to safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, and customer outcomes.
* Drive measurable gains in OEE, first-pass yield, scrap and rework, on-time delivery, lead time, inventory turns, customer response time, and total cost of quality.
* Make sure improvement work is well scoped, resourced, and sustained, and bring the best practices from inside and outside Restek to every team.

Make an Impact Across the Business

* **Manufacturing:**
  Improve safety, quality, throughput, changeover, and productivity through standard work, visual management, and a Lean production system.
* **Customer Experience:**
  Help deliver an industry-leading experience through faster response and resolution, better processes, and digital enablement.
* **Supply Chain:**
  Strengthen supplier quality and delivery, optimize inventory, and streamline order-to-cash, delivering measurable cost savings.
* **Engineering:**
  Partner on design for manufacturability, new product introduction, and change management to speed time-to-market and build it right the first time.

Build Capability and Culture

* Build, lead, and develop the Continuous Improvement team.
* Design and deliver Restek’s CI training curriculum, including Lean fundamentals, Yellow/Green/Black Belt paths, problem-solving methods, and leader standard work.
* Coach senior leaders and frontline managers in CI thinking, and develop change agents at every level to scale CI beyond the central team.
* Put the metrics and dashboards in place that make progress visible from the manufacturing floor to the executive team, and share wins and learnings across the organization.

**How We Lead at Restek**

Restek leaders model our core values and act as stewards of our culture. They communicate openly, build trust, and support the growth and well-being of their teams. They think globally and act locally, create clarity around goals, hold themselves accountable, partner across functions and regions, and lead with humility and service so every employee-owner can contribute to Restek’s success.

**What You Bring**

**Qualifications:**

The typical requirements for this role include a bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration (master's degree, preferred), or a related field, plus 10 years of progressive operations and CI experience, including at least 5 years in a senior CI or operational excellence leadership role in manufacturing, or the equivalent combination of education and experience.

**Additional Skills & Abilities:**

* A proven track record of leading enterprise-level Lean transformations with sustained, financially validated results.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification (Master Black Belt certification is preferred)
* Hands-on experience across multiple functions (manufacturing, supply chain, quality, customer service, and/or engineering), with credibility on the manufacturing floor and with leadership.
* Experience leading and developing CI practitioners and managers.
* Deep fluency in the CI toolkit: Lean (5S, standard work, visual management, flow, pull, SMED, TPM, Kaizen), Six Sigma (DMAIC, SPC, DOE), Value Stream Mapping, Hoshin Kanri, and structured problem solving (A3, 8D, 5-Why, fishbone).
* Advanced Excel and Power BI (or equivalent) skills for data-driven decision making.
* A servant-leader and coach who thinks strategically, executes in detail, and influences from the manufacturing floor to the Leadership Team, with outstanding written, verbal, and executive presentation skills.

Experience in a regulated manufacturing environment (e.g., FDA, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, GMP) or in scientific instruments, life sciences, chromatography, analytical, or precision-manufactured products and experience bringing digital tools and analytics (e.g., MES, ERP, Power BI, advanced analytics) into the CI toolkit is preferred.

This full onsite position will require the successful completion of a standard background check in accordance with Restek policy. Employment with Restek will require successful completion of a pre-employment drug screen.

**What Makes Restek Unique**

We prioritize work-life balance and well-being with offerings like generous PTO, unlimited sick time, onsite fitness center and wellness program with incentives, childcare reimbursement, and adoption assistance—giving you the tools to Own Your Well-Being. Through our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) and robust 8% retirement contributions, you can Own Your Financial Future while sharing in the success you help create. Our commitment to development ensures you can Own Your Growth through learning opportunities, career advancement programs, and a collaborative culture that values innovation and teamwork.

At Restek, our core values—We Care, Better Every Day, Respect for All, and Win Together—are at the heart of everything we do. We care deeply about our employee-owners, our customers, and the communities we serve around the world. We strive to be better every day by fostering personal and professional growth while delivering solutions that drive positive global change. We value respect for all, creating a workplace where every voice matters and diverse perspectives drive innovation. And we believe we win together, celebrating shared success as a 100% employee-owned company.

We are an equal opportunity employer, considering applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, religion, military or veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Restek provides reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and applicable laws.

If you’re ready to join a team that lives its values and empowers you to Own Your Future, we’d love to hear your story. Apply today.

**Location:**
North of Boston, MA (on-site)
  
  
**About The Company**
Our client is a growing, private equity-backed food manufacturer producing fresh, ready-to-cook proteins and meal solutions for leading grocery retailers and foodservice customers nationwide. Their products, including hand-crafted, value-added meats combined with fresh vegetables and seasonings, have earned a strong position in the specialty section of the grocery store. The company is growing, and leadership is now investing in operational excellence to support the next phase of that growth.
  
  
The Opportunity
  
  
This is a newly created role and the company's first dedicated continuous improvement leader. You'll partner closely with plant leadership to build a CI function from the ground up across a 250-person production floor. The operation is high-mix and labor-intensive: much of the product is assembled by hand, the product is perishable, and daily needs change based on customer demand. This is not machine-paced manufacturing, and it calls for someone who knows how to improve operations where people, not equipment, drive output.
  
  
Leadership is excited about this role and fully behind it. The right person will have the independence and support to make a real, measurable impact on cost, yield, and how work gets done.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  

* Lead cost-out initiatives across the plant, with a focus on labor productivity, yield, and waste reduction
* Build the KPI and metrics foundation the operation currently lacks, including labor standards, yield tracking, and performance dashboards
* Shorten the loop between labor planning and actual results so the team can manage to standard daily
* Rethink how manual work is organized and performed, including line layout, staffing models, work methods, and labor standards for high-mix hand assembly
* Identify and attack sources of product loss, giveaway, and waste in a perishable environment
* Drive structured root cause analysis and make sure fixes stick
* Introduce practical Lean and Six Sigma tools and build a CI culture where none exists today
* Work hands-on on the floor alongside supervisors and team members, coaching and training as you go
* Partner with quality and food safety to make sure improvements support regulatory and customer requirements
* Use NetSuite and Power BI to turn operational data into clear, actionable reporting

What We're Looking For
  
  

* 5+ years of continuous improvement, operational excellence, or industrial engineering experience in manufacturing, with progressive leadership responsibility
* Proven success improving labor-intensive, high-mix, manual assembly operations. This is the most important requirement.
* Food manufacturing experience strongly preferred, especially fresh, perishable, or protein processing environments
* Strong working knowledge of Lean and Six Sigma. Green Belt or Black Belt certification preferred.
* A track record of building metrics, labor standards, and accountability systems from scratch
* Documented cost savings and yield improvements you can speak to in detail
* An independent, self-directed style: someone who can assess an operation, set a plan, and execute without a lot of structure around them
* A hands-on leader who is comfortable on the production floor and earns credibility with frontline teams
* Experience with NetSuite and Power BI, or similar ERP and BI tools
* Bilingual in English and Spanish is a strong plus
* Must be local to the Greater Boston / North Shore area or willing to relocate. This role is on-site.

Why This Role
  
  

* Build the CI function from the ground up with real ownership and visible impact
* Leadership and investors who are committed to the investment and eager to support it
* A growing company with room for advancement as the business scales

Description:

The **Director of Quality & Compliance** is responsible for leading LOPA’s overall quality strategy, overseeing the agency’s Quality Management System (QMS) and ensuring that all products, services, and internal processes meet or exceed internal and external customer expectations and regulatory standards. Reporting to the Chief Strategy Officer, the position partners with operational leaders to translate requirements and quality findings into effective, measurable practices, fostering an agency-wide culture of integrity and operational excellence.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Quality Strategy & QMS Governance**

* **Quality Management System.** Own, maintain, and continuously improve the agency-wide QMS aligning objectives with organizational priorities and applicable standards.
* **Program Implementation**. Lead implementation and standardization of quality initiatives, establish milestones and accountabilities, monitor adoption, and assess ongoing effectiveness and sustainability.
* **Policies.** Oversee agency-wide development, implementation, including version control, approval workflows for all controlled documents. Support operational owners on content development and enforcement of policies and procedures.

**Regulatory Compliance & Audits**

* **Compliance Oversight.** Monitor compliance with applicable CMS requirements, OPTN policies and FDA regulations and other relevant industry standards and local and federal government regulations.
* **Audit Readiness and Management.** Oversee internal quality audits of donation and business processes to ensure regulatory and policy compliance, leveraging operational data to advise internal stakeholders on corrective actions; ensure ongoing monitoring of implemented changes to assess long-term effectiveness and sustainability. Serve as the primary liaison during external regulatory inspections and customer audits. Oversee agency’s response to any findings or observations from external audit.
* **Quality records.** Ensure quality records and compliance documentation are accurate, controlled, retrievable and inspection ready.

**Continuous Improvement & CAPA**

* **Root-Cause Analysis.** Oversees LOPA’s Occurrence Management Program to investigate instances of procedural non-conformance, resolve systemic issues, and prevent recurrence.
* **Data and KPIs.** Establish quality metrics, track key performance indicators (KPIs), and analyze statistical trends to identify efficiency gains within the QMS.
* **Support Process Optimization.** Partner with Operations leadership and the Performance Excellence team to embed quality and drive excellence in all process improvement initiatives.

**Leadership & Supplier Management**

* **Team Development.** Recruit, coach develop and evaluate a team of auditors and quality team members by setting priorities and performance expectations.
* **Supplier Quality.** Oversee vendor qualification, auditing, and performance monitoring to ensure specifications are met.
* **Customer Relations.** Collaborate directly with customers to resolve quality complaints, review technical specifications, and improve satisfaction.
* **Escalation:** Promptly communicates significant quality or regulatory concerns to CSO and recommend protective or corrective measures.

Requirements:

**Degree.** Bachelor’s degree in Quality Management, Life Sciences, Public Health, Business, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.

**Experience.** Minimum of five (5) years of progressive experience in quality management, assurance and/or control, regulatory compliance, auditing or related functions within a highly regulated environment, including at least two (2) years of supervisor, management or demonstrated functional leadership experience.

**Implementation Experience.** Demonstrated experience implementing, managing or enhancing quality management systems, regulatory compliance programs, or organization quality initiatives required.

**Industry Background.** Proven track record of applying knowledge of the principles of quality assurance/quality control. Experience within healthcare or donation and transplantation preferred.

**Skills & Certifications.** Certified Quality Manager (ASQ CMQ/OE), Six Sigma Black Belt, or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) strongly preferred.

**Technical Expertise.** Deep working knowledge of senior leadership of a Quality System. Experience applying CMS, OPTN, and FDA standards and regulations preferred.

**Leadership.** Exceptional cross-functional communication, strong decision making and problem-solving capabilities; analytical thinker with keen ability to resolve conflict and influence executive stakeholders, adept at managing agency-wide change.

Overview:

**East Tennessee Behavioral Health** is seeking a dynamic and experienced **Director of Quality and Accreditation** to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**East Tennessee Behavioral Healt**h is a 90-bed inpatient treatment center serving Knoxville, Tennessee, and the surrounding communities. We provide the highest-quality care for people who have mental health concerns such as depression, anxiety disorders, and bipolar disorder and those who have co-occurring addictions. The acute inpatient treatment we offer supports adolescents, adults, and senior adults, while our outpatient programming serves adults age 18 and older.

**East TN Behavioral Health Hospital** offers an extensive array of benefits to our valued team members. Current offerings encompass:

* Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance coverage
* Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) options
* Company-paid Basic Life & AD&D insurance
* Disability benefits
* 401(k) Retirement Plan with a company match
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and Employee Discount Program
* Paid Holidays for work-life balance
* Paid Time Off (PTO)
* Tuition Reimbursement opportunities for career advancement

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
  + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
  + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
  + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
  + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
  + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
  + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
  + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
  + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.
* Regulatory preparedness – implement sustainable survey preparation and ongoing monitoring processes, including facility-wide auditing and early-issue identification, to maximize achievement of zero- or standard-level survey outcomes.
  + Facility-wide support – collaborate with other departments to sustainably implement best-practices in regulatory/accreditation compliance as evidenced by measurable results with regard to survey outcomes, patient safety metrics, patient experience results, HBIPS, etc.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in regulatory planning strategy for all standards for all relevant regulatory and accrediting bodies at the local, state, and federal level.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in the functionality and auditing within electronic platforms such as electronic patient observations and the electronic medical record, as applicable.
  + Lead Root-Cause Analyses and conduct timely and regular evaluation of serious incidents, complaints, grievances and related investigations to:
    - Identification of events, trends and patterns that may affect client health, safety and or treatment efficacy,
    - Committee evaluation findings and recommendations submitted to agency management for corrective action,
    - Implemented actions, outcomes, trends analyzed over time
  + Develop corrective action plans for the resolution of areas of regulatory vulnerability or those which could compromise patient safety in collaboration with other facility leaders.
  + Ensure proper reporting of violations or potential violations to duly authorized enforcement agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + Ensure proper reporting of incidents and adverse clinical outcomes to duly authorized enforcement agencies or regulatory agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + In conjunction with assigned corporate Division Quality Director, initiate and lead communications with regulatory agencies as appropriate.
  + Develop sustainable performance improvement practices through analysis of data and prioritization of efforts to improve survey readiness and consistency of care delivery using expected best-practices.
  + Ensure multidisciplinary ownership of best-practices in self-monitoring, auditing, and process improvement, escalating opportunities for improved engagement to the facility CEO as appropriate.
  + Ensures strategic and operational implementation of regulatory requirements, guidelines, and standards of federal, state, and local licensing agencies, accrediting and certifying organizations.
  + Collaborates with Division and Corporate entities and external parties to ensure strategic quality and patient safety initiatives are fully executed at the facility level. Facilitates effective communication with facility and division leadership regarding key clinical performance improvement activities and initiatives.
  + Serves as a technical advisor, educator and internal consultant to all hospital management, staff, and physicians on the use of performance improvement tools and techniques, analytical techniques, and statistical applications.
  + Ensure facility compliance with policies and applicable standards as required by regulatory/accrediting bodies.
  + Facility leader and subject matter expert on high reliability principles and strategies to achieve zero harm.

* Clinical program excellence – assess fidelity and identify root-causes for gaps/lapses in fidelity to Acadia standards. Support other departments in developing and implementing remediation and improvement plans to achieve fidelity to Acadia’s expected practices, including all elements of treatment program implementation.
* + Develop, review, and educate on internal clinical procedures and appropriate use of outcome evaluation tools and the associated results – including patient experience data and other quality scorecard metrics – to ensure continuous quality improvement and ongoing compliance with federal, state, and third-party regulatory requirements.
  + Translate standards, requirements, and policies into terms or processes meaningful to the facility.
* Leadership – serve as a visible, engaged, and dynamic member of the facility leadership team.
  + Chairs the monthly Quality Council
  + Complete safety rounds, participate in leadership rounding, and submit results/corrective actions to Acadia corporate office.
  + Review incident/safety concerns with the leadership team to identify systemic issues and facilitate the development of corrective actions.
  + Lead and facilitate Root Cause Analyses into all serious and/or sentinel events.
  + Invest in the facility staff through engagement in hiring, development, training, performance management, and communication to ensure effective and efficient operations.
  + Oversees the Culture of Safety Survey and follow-up action planning and sustainment processes.
  + Identification of problems or potential problems to prevent risks to patients and staff. Proposes corrective steps that may include, but are not limited to:
    - Changes in policies/procedures,
    - Staffing and assignment changes,
    - Additional education or training for staff,
    - Addition or deletion of services

**OTHER FUNCTIONS:**

* Perform other functions and tasks as assigned.

Qualifications:

**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Human Services or nursing required. Master’s degree in behavioral health/risk discipline, Registered Nurse preferred.
* Two or more years of experience in a Quality, Clinical, or PI role required.
* One or more years of management experience preferred.
* Experience with CARF, DEA, Joint Commission, or CMS surveys, as required by service line(s) supported

**LICENSES/DESIGNATIONS/CERTIFICATIONS:**

* Current licensure appropriate for the degree held required.
* CPR and de-escalation/restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).
* First aid may be required based on state or facility.

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.**  
  
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

The role offers the opportunity to influence the quality standard for a growing federal business and help prepare the organization to support additional federal programs over time.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.

Overview:

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Director of Quality and Accreditation to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
  + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
  + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
  + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
  + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
  + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
  + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
  + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
  + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.
* Regulatory preparedness – implement sustainable survey preparation and ongoing monitoring processes, including facility-wide auditing and early-issue identification, to maximize achievement of zero- or standard-level survey outcomes.
  + Facility-wide support – collaborate with other departments to sustainably implement best-practices in regulatory/accreditation compliance as evidenced by measurable results with regard to survey outcomes, patient safety metrics, patient experience results, HBIPS, etc.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in regulatory planning strategy for all standards for all relevant regulatory and accrediting bodies at the local, state, and federal level.
  + Develop and maintain proficiency in the functionality and auditing within electronic platforms such as electronic patient observations and the electronic medical record, as applicable.
  + Lead Root-Cause Analyses and conduct timely and regular evaluation of serious incidents, complaints, grievances and related investigations to:
    - Identification of events, trends and patterns that may affect client health, safety and or treatment efficacy,
    - Committee evaluation findings and recommendations submitted to agency management for corrective action,
    - Implemented actions, outcomes, trends analyzed over time
  + Develop corrective action plans for the resolution of areas of regulatory vulnerability or those which could compromise patient safety in collaboration with other facility leaders.
  + Ensure proper reporting of violations or potential violations to duly authorized enforcement agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + Ensure proper reporting of incidents and adverse clinical outcomes to duly authorized enforcement agencies or regulatory agencies as appropriate and/or required.
  + In conjunction with assigned corporate Division Quality Director, initiate and lead communications with regulatory agencies as appropriate.
  + Develop sustainable performance improvement practices through analysis of data and prioritization of efforts to improve survey readiness and consistency of care delivery using expected best-practices.
  + Ensure multidisciplinary ownership of best-practices in self-monitoring, auditing, and process improvement, escalating opportunities for improved engagement to the facility CEO as appropriate.
  + Ensures strategic and operational implementation of regulatory requirements, guidelines, and standards of federal, state, and local licensing agencies, accrediting and certifying organizations.
  + Collaborates with Division and Corporate entities and external parties to ensure strategic quality and patient safety initiatives are fully executed at the facility level. Facilitates effective communication with facility and division leadership regarding key clinical performance improvement activities and initiatives.
  + Serves as a technical advisor, educator and internal consultant to all hospital management, staff, and physicians on the use of performance improvement tools and techniques, analytical techniques, and statistical applications.
  + Ensure facility compliance with policies and applicable standards as required by regulatory/accrediting bodies.
  + Facility leader and subject matter expert on high reliability principles and strategies to achieve zero harm.

* Clinical program excellence – assess fidelity and identify root-causes for gaps/lapses in fidelity to Acadia standards. Support other departments in developing and implementing remediation and improvement plans to achieve fidelity to Acadia’s expected practices, including all elements of treatment program implementation.
* + Develop, review, and educate on internal clinical procedures and appropriate use of outcome evaluation tools and the associated results – including patient experience data and other quality scorecard metrics – to ensure continuous quality improvement and ongoing compliance with federal, state, and third-party regulatory requirements.
  + Translate standards, requirements, and policies into terms or processes meaningful to the facility.
* Leadership – serve as a visible, engaged, and dynamic member of the facility leadership team.
  + Chairs the monthly Quality Council
  + Complete safety rounds, participate in leadership rounding, and submit results/corrective actions to Acadia corporate office.
  + Review incident/safety concerns with the leadership team to identify systemic issues and facilitate the development of corrective actions.
  + Lead and facilitate Root Cause Analyses into all serious and/or sentinel events.
  + Invest in the facility staff through engagement in hiring, development, training, performance management, and communication to ensure effective and efficient operations.
  + Oversees the Culture of Safety Survey and follow-up action planning and sustainment processes.
  + Identification of problems or potential problems to prevent risks to patients and staff. Proposes corrective steps that may include, but are not limited to:
    - Changes in policies/procedures,
    - Staffing and assignment changes,
    - Additional education or training for staff,
    - Addition or deletion of services

**OTHER FUNCTIONS:**

* Perform other functions and tasks as assigned.

Qualifications:

**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Human Services or nursing required. Master’s degree in behavioral health/risk discipline, Registered Nurse preferred.
* Two or more years of experience in a Quality, Clinical, or PI role required.
* One or more years of management experience preferred.
* Experience with CARF, DEA, Joint Commission, or CMS surveys, as required by service line(s) supported

**LICENSES/DESIGNATIONS/CERTIFICATIONS:**

* Current licensure appropriate for the degree held required.
* CPR and de-escalation/restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).
* First aid may be required based on state or facility.

**ADDITIONAL REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS:**

***While this job description is intended to be*** ***an accurate*** ***reflection of the requirements of the job, management reserves the right to add or remove duties from*** ***par******ticular jobs*** ***when circumstances***  
***(******e.g.*** ***emergencies, changes in workload, rush jobs or technological developments) dictate.***

At Vestis®, we provide uniforms, workplace supplies, and professional cleaning that help businesses simplify their workday and keep their teams safe, confident, and focused on what matters most. More than a provider, we are a partner in productivity, trusted to keep you running.
  
Join us and build a career supporting the people who make it all work.
  
  
Overview
  
The Vice President of Distribution Center Operations will lead the product distribution strategy and drive an economically competitive operation that delivers both best-in-class customer experience and distribution cost advantages across all facilities supporting Vestis Rental and Direct Sale customers.
  
This leader will influence and reinforce a portfolio of core values and accountability standards centered on safety, workforce engagement, customer experience, operational efficiency, and innovative solutions that support business goals. This role is responsible for deploying strategies and actionable plans that deliver measurable performance improvement.
  
This leader will also define and advance the technology roadmap for Distribution Center Operations, identifying opportunities to leverage artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, automation, advanced analytics, and other emerging technologies to improve safety, productivity, quality, service, capacity, and cost.
  
The Vice President will promote data-driven performance visibility, real-time corrective action, and strong cross-functional collaboration. This leader will work effectively with business partners to identify, address, and resolve operational issues.
  
This role will set goals and oversee key metrics related to customer fill rates, customer satisfaction, footprint utilization, inventory management, optimization and total DC cost, along with other key measures tied to Distribution Center Operations.
  
Responsibilities/Essential Functions
  

* Set and deliver the overall vision and distribution strategy for national and international distribution centers to ensure end-to-end customer needs are met at the lowest possible cost.
* Lead a high-performing team of supply chain practitioners, with direct and indirect responsibility for an organization of more than 600 employees.
* Partner with Human Resources to design and implement workforce strategies for each distribution center location, including the evolution of workforce skills needed to support increasingly automated and technology-enabled operations.
* Define objectives, establish key performance metrics, and create a regular review cadence across safety, quality, fill rate, customer satisfaction, inventory management, budget performance, and other critical operating areas.
* Implement metrics, processes, and operating routines that drive accountability and ensure results.
* Improve costs year over year through disciplined operational execution and continuous improvement.
* Drive performance improvement through the use of continuous improvement methodology.
* Build strong cross-functional partnerships to identify, escalate, and resolve operational issues and improvement opportunities.

* Manage domestic and international direct and indirect reporting teams to ensure processes and procedures are consistent across all facilities.
* Lead the annual budgeting process in partnership with DC Operations and Direct Sale Finance Teams and Sales Leadership.
* Stay current on information, technology, and trends affecting functional areas; promote innovation and make appropriate recommendations to executive leadership.
* Develop and execute a multi-year distribution technology and automation roadmap, including the evaluation and adoption of AI, robotics, material-handling automation, advanced analytics, and emerging distribution technologies where they provide measurable operational and financial value.
* Evaluate opportunities to automate manual and repetitive processes across receiving, put-away, inventory movement, picking, packing, sortation, shipping, and related distribution workflows.
* Establish business cases and success measures for major automation and technology investments, including productivity improvement, service impact, safety, capacity, labor requirements, operating cost, capital requirements, and return on investment.
* Partner with Information Technology, Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, Human Resources, and external technology partners to successfully pilot, scale, and operationalize new distribution technologies across the network.
* Use data, predictive analytics, and AI-enabled decision support to improve demand and capacity planning, inventory positioning, workforce planning, asset utilization, operational visibility, and decision-making.
* Build a culture of innovation in which technology augments the workforce, improves safety and efficiency, and prepares the distribution organization for future operating requirements.
* Set the overall strategy for operational performance planning to drive quality standards and efficiency.
* Oversee and monitor safety and security in accordance with national and international requirements for facilities and employees. Ensure proper training and adherence to company requirements.
* Drive employment decisions and recommendations, including hiring, retention, improvement plans, transfers, promotions, corrective actions, terminations, and pay adjustments.
* Manage employee performance and support improvement through coaching, mentoring, and formal performance reviews.
* Recommend, plan, and implement employee training and skill development activities.
* Lead communication on company and departmental issues, priorities, and goals. Provide oversight of employee growth and development through weekly team meetings, regular one-on-one meetings, coaching, performance management, training, and company-sponsored learning opportunities.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities
  

* Demonstrated understanding of technical issues within a global distribution framework.
* Strong understanding of modern distribution technologies, including warehouse automation, robotics, AI, machine learning applications, advanced analytics, and automated material-handling solutions.
* Ability to translate emerging technology into practical operational use cases and measurable business outcomes rather than implementing technology for technology’s sake.
* Strong understanding of automation investment strategy, including business-case development, scalability, change management, operational readiness, and return on investment.
* Ability to lead transformation in environments where automated and traditional operations may need to coexist across different facilities.
* Strong project leadership and cross-functional leadership experience.
* Ability to think, plan, and execute strategically.
* Ability to influence and build consensus with executive leadership.
* Comfortable operating in ambiguity.
* Decisive and persuasive, with a strong sense of urgency and a proven ability to drive results.
* Strong organizational skills.
* Excellent analytical skills and technical capabilities.
* Willingness and ability to travel extensively, both nationally and internationally.

Working Environment/Safety Requirements
  
Role is based in Lawrenceville, GA.
  
Requires up to 50% travel across the U.S. and Canada.
  
Work includes distribution center, plant, and office environments, including corporate office interaction in Roswell, GA.
  
Must comply with all company safety, security, and site-specific requirements.
  
Experience/Qualifications
  

* 15 years of experience leading a large workforce in a high-volume, fast-paced global distribution or manufacturing network.
* Bachelor’s degree in business, supply chain operations, engineering, or a related field required; MBA preferred.
* Recognized thought leader and expert within business, supply chain, logistics, and/or global distribution disciplines.

* Experience evaluating automation technologies and building investment recommendations based on operational benefit, scalability, capital requirements, and return on investment.

About Us

  

Skydweller Aero Inc. is a transatlantic, cutting-edge aerospace company developing solar-powered aircraft solutions capable of perpetual flight while carrying heavy and powerful payloads. Building on technology from the longest continuous renewably powered flight program in history, this fast-growing company is creating a new class of unmanned aircraft. It combines the persistence of geosynchronous satellites with the sensing capabilities and flexibility of a large airborne platform. Skydweller Aero Inc. has its global and US headquarters in Oklahoma City, with European operations headquartered in Spain.

Role Summary

  

As Skydweller prepares to move from development toward aircraft production, we are looking for an experienced manufacturing executive to build and lead our production organization. This role is based in **Oklahoma City, OK** and reports to the Chief Operating Officer.

The Vice President, Manufacturing & Production will own all aircraft production operations: final assembly, systems integration, avionics installation, production testing, factory operations and aircraft delivery. You will lead the organization as we scale from prototype and low-rate initial production into sustained manufacturing.

We are looking for a hands-on aerospace manufacturing leader with a proven track record of building production organizations, improving factory performance and delivering complex aircraft in FAA-regulated environments.

**Why join:** Most manufacturing leadership roles optimize an existing production system. This one builds it. You will establish the manufacturing organization, develop the factory workforce, and scale production of one of the most ambitious autonomous aircraft programs in aerospace.

Responsibilities

  

**Production leadership**

  

* Lead all aircraft production and manufacturing operations.
* Drive safe, efficient and repeatable aircraft production.
* Build and lead a high-performing manufacturing organization, with clear management systems, metrics and operating rhythms.
* Foster a culture of accountability, safety, quality and continuous improvement.

  

**Assembly and integration**

* Oversee final assembly, systems and electrical integration, avionics installation and aircraft completion.
* Ensure aircraft are built to engineering, quality and regulatory requirements.
* Drive production readiness and resolve manufacturing constraints and bottlenecks.

  

**Production planning and execution**

* Own execution of the Master Production Schedule.
* Lead production planning, labor allocation and resource management.
* Set capacity plans that support production-rate growth.
* Monitor factory performance and drive throughput, productivity and efficiency improvements.

  

**Production testing and acceptance**

* Lead production acceptance testing and ground test operations.
* Coordinate production readiness with Engineering, Quality, Flight Operations and Program Management.
* Ensure aircraft move smoothly from production through acceptance and delivery.

  

**Regulatory compliance and quality**

* Ensure compliance with FAA Part 21 production requirements and the company quality management system.
* Maintain production configuration control and manufacturing documentation discipline.
* Support internal, regulatory and customer audits and certification activities.
* Partner with Quality leadership to improve first-pass yield.

  

**Growth and scale-up**

* Develop the manufacturing infrastructure, facilities and staffing plans needed for higher production rates.
* Implement lean manufacturing and operational excellence initiatives.

  

**People leadership**

* Recruit, develop and mentor production leaders and technical staff.
* Establish workforce development and skills-training programs.
* Build strong partnerships across Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Flight Operations and Program Management.

  

Success Measures

You will be measured on aircraft delivery performance, production schedule attainment, factory throughput, labor productivity, manufacturing cost, quality and first-pass yield, safety, production-rate readiness, and workforce development and retention.

Required Qualifications

  

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Aerospace, Operations or a related technical field.
* 15+ years of progressive aerospace manufacturing leadership experience, including 10+ years leading production organizations in aerospace, defense, aviation or another highly regulated industry.
* Proven experience scaling manufacturing from development, prototype or low-rate production to higher-rate production.
* Experience leading large, cross-functional manufacturing organizations.
* Strong understanding of production planning, factory operations, quality systems and manufacturing performance metrics.
* Experience implementing lean manufacturing and operational excellence initiatives.
* Excellent communication, leadership and organizational skills.

  

Preferred Qualifications

  

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Business or Operations.
* FAA Part 21 production experience and experience with certified aircraft manufacturing programs.
* Experience leading final assembly and aircraft integration organizations.
* Experience supporting aircraft certification, conformity and production acceptance.
* Background in autonomous aircraft, UAS, defense aviation or advanced aerospace systems.
* Experience building greenfield or fast-growing manufacturing operations.
* Composite aircraft manufacturing experience.
* AS9100 quality system experience.

  

Please Note

  

* **Security clearance requirement:** This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance. U.S. citizenship is required.

* **One application per candidate:** Please apply to one position only. If you are interested in other open roles, list them in the Notes section of your application.

* **Check your spam folder:** We use BambooHR, a third-party recruiting platform, to contact candidates. Please check your spam or junk folder regularly so you don't miss our messages.

* **English CV:** Please submit your resume in English.

  

Company Benefits

  

* **Health insurance:** Medical, dental and vision coverage for all full-time employees.
* **401(k) retirement plan:** A 401(k) plan to help you save for retirement.
* **Paid time off:** Vacation, sick leave and personal days.
* **Flexible schedules:** Flexible working hours to support a healthy work-life balance.
* **Professional development:** Training, education and tuition reimbursement opportunities to help you grow your skills and career.
* **Wellness programs:** Programs that support healthy living, which may include gym memberships, nutrition counseling or stress-management classes.
* **Stock options:** Full-time employees may be eligible for stock options after one year of service.
* **Performance bonuses:** Bonus opportunities that reward individual and company performance.

  

Equal Opportunity Employer

Skydweller Aero Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law, subject to the security clearance requirements above.

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us at [email].

Privacy and AI

existing_roles.description:
**Overview**

The Vice President of Quality provides strategic leadership and oversight of all quality functions, ensuring products and manufacturing processes meet customer requirements, applicable quality standards, and company expectations. This position is responsible for developing and executing the company's quality strategy, maintaining an effective quality management system, driving continuous improvement, and ensuring customer satisfaction.

The VP of Quality partners with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to improve manufacturing performance, reduce quality-related costs, resolve complex quality issues, and establish a culture of accountability and operational excellence.

Direct semiconductor manufacturing experience is required. The successful candidate must have 10–15 years of progressive quality experience, including experience in semiconductor equipment manufacturing, with a demonstrated ability to lead quality initiatives and deliver measurable improvements in product quality, process performance, and customer satisfaction.

**Duties**

- Develop and implement the company's quality strategy, objectives, and improvement initiatives in alignment with business goals.

- Provide executive leadership and oversight for all Quality department functions, personnel, systems, and processes.

- Establish, implement, and maintain an effective quality management system in accordance with applicable ISO standards, customer requirements, and industry standards.

- Ensure products and manufacturing processes meet established specifications, customer expectations, and applicable quality requirements.

- Serve as a senior point of contact for customer quality concerns, escalations, audits, corrective actions, and quality performance reviews.

- Manage root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and continuous improvement initiatives to prevent recurring quality issues.

- Establish and monitor key quality performance indicators, identify trends, and implement improvement plans to reduce defects, scrap, rework, and quality-related costs.

- Partner with Operations, Engineering, Production, and other departments to resolve manufacturing issues and improve process consistency.

- Oversee internal and external quality audits, supplier quality performance, nonconformance management, and compliance activities.

- Ensure appropriate quality resources, inspection equipment, measurement systems, work instructions, and technical documentation are available and maintained.

- Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Quality organization with clear performance expectations, accountability, and development plans.

- Promote a culture of quality, teamwork, continuous improvement, and shared responsibility across the organization.

- Report quality performance, significant risks, customer concerns, and improvement initiatives to executive leadership.

- Evaluate quality risks and make sound decisions using technical analysis, available data, customer impact, and business priorities.

- Identify opportunities to improve process efficiency, reduce waste, and optimize the use of company resources.

- Maintain effective communication and coordination among Quality, Manufacturing, customers, and suppliers.

- Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Required Knowledge and Skills

- Extensive knowledge of quality assurance, quality engineering, quality management systems, and manufacturing process controls.

- Direct knowledge and experience with semiconductor manufacturing quality requirements and production processes.

- Strong understanding of statistical process control (SPC), process capability studies, metrology, statistical analysis, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive action methodologies.

- Experience implementing quality systems, managing audits, and driving continuous improvement.

- Ability to interpret technical specifications, engineering drawings, inspection requirements, and manufacturing documentation.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex issues and implement effective solutions.

- Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams, influence stakeholders, and establish accountability throughout an organization.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present technical findings and quality performance to executive leadership, customers, and employees.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and quality reporting and data analysis tools.

- Ability to balance customer expectations, product quality, operational efficiency, and business objectives.

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or a related technical field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

- 7–10 years of progressive quality engineering and quality leadership experience, including direct experience in semiconductor equipment manufacturing.

-Black belt or Green belt certification.

- Semiconductor manufacturing experience is mandatory. General manufacturing quality experience alone does not meet this requirement.

- Demonstrated experience leading quality functions or significant quality initiatives within a semiconductor manufacturing environment.

- Experience with manufacturing process controls, defect reduction, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and continuous improvement.

- Experience managing customer quality requirements, customer and supplier audits, nonconformances, and corrective action programs.

- Proven ability to lead and develop teams, establish strategic priorities, and deliver measurable improvements in product quality and customer satisfaction.

- Strong leadership, organizational, communication, and decision-making skills.

**Responsibility for Work of Others**

Provides executive leadership and oversight for the Quality department, including Quality managers, supervisors, engineers, inspectors, and other quality personnel, as applicable. Establishes departmental objectives, assigns responsibilities, evaluates performance, and ensures adequate staffing, training, and resources to meet company and customer requirements.

**Additional Information**

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed in this position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or qualifications. Additional responsibilities may be assigned as business needs require.

* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
